| Repetition under the same conditions | Task, brief, model settings, execution policy | The parts of generation that cannot be pinned down. | Several trials of the same task. | Each arm received a byte-identical packet ten times. |

| Usage policy | What question it answers | Conditions | Hypothetical value (p=0.8) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Run once and adopt the result | How reliable one delivery is | Carries the assumption above that each run has p=0.8 | 80% |
| Deliver three times in a row, adopt each one | The chance that none of the three goes wrong (pass^3) | Nobody selects or intercepts in between | 0.8³ = 51.2% |
| Run three times and pick the one that succeeded | At least one usable result in three (pass@3) | A selector that can recognize success; all three runs are paid for | 1 − 0.2³ = 99.2% |
| Run in sequence and stop at the first success | Same as above, with fewer attempts spent | The selector can judge each attempt immediately | 99.2%, 1.24 attempts on average |

|---|---|---|---|---|
| X | Five tasks passed both times, the other five failed both times | 10/20 | 5/10 | 5/10 |
| Y | All ten tasks passed once and failed once | 10/20 | 0/10 | 10/10 |

| Problem | What it looks like | Next piece of evidence | What cannot substitute |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not enough data | The interval for the difference crosses the practical threshold | Plan the number of tasks, repetitions and precision in advance, from the effect to be estimated, task differences and same-task dependence | Deciding to add more after seeing the results |
| Observations cannot discriminate | All arms pass every trial, or all arms fail every trial | Tasks that represent the target work and have a chance of revealing differences, or other outcomes fixed in advance | Adding runs only to wait for the arms to separate; picking only harder tasks. |
| Requirements differ between conditions | The conditions differ in requirements beyond the component being compared | Align the requirements first, then regenerate | Adding samples for the old packet |
| The task does not represent the target work | The study task differs from the work that actually comes in | Build a sampling frame from the incoming work list, keeping the reasons for exclusion | Rewriting tasks whose answers are already disclosed into "new" ones |
| The yardstick cannot see | Legitimate variation is rejected, or a known faulty version gets through | Fix the oracle, add positive and negative controls (outputs that must be accepted and known faulty versions that must be rejected), re-score the existing candidates consistently | Generating more candidates |
| Human cost unknown | Only model cost and structural descriptions | Records of a person taking over, and deep reads sampled in advance | AST similarity, review by an AI agent, model list prices |

| Reviewer's question | formal-01-A0 | formal-02-A0 | What this reading can confirm |
|---|---|---|---|
| Where is `text: false` rejected? | The agent-message branch in `main` (lines 115–125): handle null first, then reject non-strings, then exclude the empty string, and finally count the message and print it | `_handle_item` (lines 83–91): handle null and the empty string first, then reject non-strings, and finally count the message and print it | Both can point to the R05 path, but the order of the checks differs |
| How does a bad line affect what follows and EOF? | Lines 73–80 keep malformed in a dict inside the function; completion, spoken message and failure are other local variables; `malformed()` updates the dict and prints the diagnostic | `_State` at lines 26–31 holds all four states in one place; `_malformed` at lines 60–63 updates the object and prints the diagnostic; every handler shares the same object | The state lives in different places, so the trail to follow differs |
| Why does explicit failure come before malformed? | The EOF branch at lines 189–200 checks failure first, then malformed, then completion and spoken message | Lines 223–233 decide in the order failure, malformed, completion, spoken message | Both lead directly to R11's decision order |

| What changed | What to reconfirm | Regenerate? |
|---|---|---|
| Requirements or compatibility responsibilities revised | Re-derive the expected values and the positive and negative controls; decide which old results no longer apply | Not needed to re-score existing artifacts; needed to compare the delivery method under the new brief. |
| Grader revised | Check the new yardstick with the verified positive and negative control fixtures. | Not needed. |
| A new patch appears | Check this candidate with the contract cases | Not needed; the candidate already exists |
| Model, harness or tool policy changed | The new method's distribution of results on the applicable tasks | Needed |
